properties.name: Clifton Suspension Bridge
properties.funFact: Designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel, the bridge opened in 1864 and uses iron chains originally built for London's Hungerford Bridge.

properties.name: Brunel's SS Great Britain
properties.funFact: Launched in Bristol in 1843, she was the world's first ocean liner to combine an iron hull with a screw propeller.

properties.name: Cabot Tower (Brandon Hill)
properties.funFact: Built in 1897 to mark 400 years since John Cabot sailed from Bristol to North America, its spiral staircase climbs 105 feet.

properties.name: Castle Park & St Peter's Church
properties.funFact: The ruined shell of St Peter's Church has been preserved as a permanent memorial to the Bristol Blitz of November 1940.

properties.name: St Nicholas Market Exchange
properties.funFact: Outside the 1743 Exchange stand four bronze 'Nails'—merchants paid cash on them, inspiring the phrase 'pay on the nail'.

properties.name: Wills Memorial Building
properties.funFact: Opened in 1925, its neo-Gothic tower houses Great George, a 9.5-tonne bell that is one of the largest in Britain.

properties.name: Troopers Hill Chimney
properties.funFact: This Grade II listed 1790s flue once served copper smelting and chemical works overlooking the River Avon in St George.

properties.name: St George Park Lake
properties.funFact: Opened in 1894 on former brickworks land, St George Park is home to one of Bristol's oldest Victorian ornamental lakes.

properties.name: Clifton Observatory & Giant's Cave
properties.funFact: Originally a 1766 snuff mill, its rooftop houses a working Victorian camera obscura projecting live panoramic views of the gorge.

properties.name: Bristol Temple Meads Old Station
properties.funFact: Completed in 1840 as the western terminus of Brunel's Great Western Railway, it is the oldest surviving railway terminus in the world.

properties.name: Snuff Mills (Frome Valley)
properties.funFact: Named after a quarryman who ground snuff here in the 18th century, its riverside waterwheel still turns beside the River Frome.

properties.name: Ashton Court Ancient Oaks
properties.funFact: Ashton Court's 850-acre estate shelters ancient veteran oak trees that are more than 700 years old.
